## 2 · Visual transmission law `[S]`

This is production law, binding on every frame, and it is **not** a portal.

### 2.1 · The law

> The world and the characters move **behind** a subtle, fixed viewing-medium
> layer. The viewing medium is **screen-relative**: it does not move with the
> camera, does not track a subject, and does not sit at any depth inside the
> scene. Subjects move behind it.

### 2.2 · Permitted expressions of the medium

Faint optical softness · aged-film or picture-tube texture · minute reflections ·
haze · micro-scratches · glass-like interference. Applied at low strength, evenly,
and with no narrative timing — the medium never "reacts".

### 2.3 · Prohibited absolutely

- **No bubble.** No portal. No force field. No visible dimension wall.
- No edge, rim, seam, boundary arc, membrane or shimmer-line that reads as the
  near face of an object.
- **No character may touch, press, reach toward, look at, flinch from, or
  otherwise perceive the medium.** If a performance implies awareness of it, the
  performance is wrong, not the medium.
- The medium may not be used as a transition, a reveal, or a WYCK manifestation.
  WYCK is internal (§4); the medium is optical. **They are never the same layer.**

### 2.4 · Note on the supplied poster

The Chairman-supplied reference poster shows a **curved luminous vertical seam**
with a second world behind it. That seam is **key-art language for the
transmission card only.** It is **not** licensed into episode frames and would
violate §2.3 if reproduced in the episode. Recorded as unresolved decision
**U-03**: whether key art keeps the seam while episode frames do not.

## 3 · Bramble — locked reference and pending changes

### 3.1 · Locked, not to be redesigned

Bramble's visual identity is the **Chairman-supplied approved reference image in
this conversation** (`ER·TX·001·BRAMBLE·V2`). The child is **not** redesigned.
Held from the reference:

- A boy of roughly nine to ten years; small, light build.
- **Realistic human facial anatomy** — ordinary child proportion, a real skull, a
  real jaw, real ears, real eye spacing.
- Freckled cheeks and nose-bridge; a slightly uneven complexion; visible fine
  hairs at the temple.
- Warm brown/hazel eyes, dark lashes, thick dark brows.
- Tousled mid-brown hair, longer at the nape, escaping at the ears.
- Slightly parted mouth in the reference — the **listening/asking** expression.
- An upward, open, curious head-tilt: **the question posture**.
- Layered, worn, working-family clothing in **browns and earth tones**, visibly
  mended and out-grown.

### 3.2 · Prohibited

- **No cartoon anatomy.** No enlarged cranium, no oversized eyes, no shrunken
  jaw, no button nose, no stylised iris, no smoothed-out skin, no doll rendering.
- No aging up or down from the reference. No change of hair colour or eye colour.
- No redesign of the face under any lighting, costume or seasonal change.

### 3.3 · Changes pending before generation

Four changes are approved and **must be applied before any generation**; nothing
else about the child changes.

| # | Change | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| **C-1** | **Deep-red period winter cap with a soft pom/ball top** | Replaces the brown tweed flat cap of the reference. Knitted wool, deep red, hand-knitted character, turned-up brim band, **soft pom/ball at the crown**. Period-correct for a 1945 English winter and consistent with clothes-rationing reality (`S-17`): knitted at home from unravelled wool, so **no coupons spent** — see `WORLD-CORVESLEY.md` §6. |
| **C-2** | **Selective deep-red scarf accents** | The scarf remains, now carrying **deep-red accents** — stripe, band or end-blocks — rather than becoming a uniformly red scarf. "Selective" is binding: red is an **accent** on the scarf, not its whole field. |
| **C-3** | **All other brown/earth clothing treatment preserved** | Coat, jersey, shirt, trousers, socks, boots and satchel stay in the reference's browns and earth tones, with the same wear, mending and fit — **unless** a specific item is historically or physically inconsistent, in which case it is corrected and the correction is logged, not applied silently. |
| **C-4** | **Realistic human facial anatomy; no cartoon anatomy** | Restated as a generation-time gate, not a style preference. Any output showing cartoon anatomy is rejected, not adjusted. |

**Red discipline:** deep red now appears in exactly two places — cap and scarf
accents. Because the rest of the palette is brown and earth, red becomes the
**tracking colour** for Bramble in a crowd, in a corridor, and in snow. No other
character in EP001 wears deep red. Recorded as a standing palette reservation.

## 4 · WYCK — manifestation law `[S]`

### 4.1 · What WYCK is in EP001

WYCK is **Bramble's inner questioning signal**. In EP001 it manifests
**subtly**. It is the thing that arrives when a fact does not sit flat — the
pull toward the next question.

### 4.2 · Held from stored canon

**WYCK talks directly to Bramble.** That capability is canon (§1.3) and is not
withdrawn. EP001 simply uses it at its **quietest register**.

### 4.3 · Manifestation rules for EP001

| Rule | Statement |
|---|---|
| W-1 | WYCK is **perceived by Bramble only**. No other child, no adult, no animal reacts to it. |
| W-2 | WYCK manifests **when a stated fact and an observed fact disagree** — never on emotion, never on danger, never on cue. |
| W-3 | The manifestation is **subtle**: a shift in the room's sound, a held beat, a small pressure behind the question. It is **not** a glow, a spirit, a creature, a second shadow, or a light. |
| W-4 | WYCK **never gives the answer.** It only marks the disagreement and returns the next question to Bramble. Anything that resolves the mystery for him breaks the character. |
| W-5 | WYCK is **never the viewing medium** (§2.3). The optical layer must not thicken, flicker, warm or move when WYCK arrives. |
| W-6 | WYCK does not accuse. When Bramble's question turns toward a person rather than a fact, **WYCK goes quiet.** This is the episode's moral engine and is load-bearing. |

### 4.4 · The question-cue

The stored canon's "subtle question-cue that most other children do not see" is
realised in EP001 as **Bramble's own physical tell** — the upward head-tilt of
the reference image (§3.1), plus a stillness of the hands. It is **his** cue,
readable by the audience, unread by the room. It is not an effect.

## 5 · Episode 001 premise

### 5.1 · The discrepancy

A classroom arithmetic exercise says **twelve** exercise books should remain in
the class stock. Physical observation finds **eleven**.

Bramble asks **why**.

WYCK manifests subtly, at its quietest register, at the moment the stated figure
and the counted figure disagree (W-2).

**The children investigate before accusing anyone.**

### 5.2 · What the episode is actually about

Not a theft. The episode is about the distance between **a record** and **a
thing** — and about the discipline of closing that distance with evidence
instead of with a name. The 1945 setting is not decoration: the school is
mid-transition under the Education Act 1944 (`S-02`), paper is a controlled
commodity that it is illegal to burn or throw away (`S-12`), and a council
salvage collection runs through the building (`S-19`). Every one of those
sourced facts makes an **innocent** explanation available. That is the point.

### 5.3 · Boundary of this bible — **the mystery is not solved here**

By instruction, this bible establishes the **physical school, the teacher, the
class, the object custody and the plausible explanations**, and stops there. It
does **not** name what happened to the twelfth book. `OBJECTS-AND-CUSTODY.md` §7
lists **eleven live candidate explanations**, each with the evidence test that
would confirm or eliminate it, and **none is marked true**. Selecting the
explanation is unresolved decision **U-01**, held for the Chairman.

## 6 · The cognitive team

Four children, four distinct instruments. No child does another's job — that
separation is the show's engine and must survive every rewrite.

| Role | Child | Instrument | Asks | Fails by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **WHY** | **Bramble** | The question that does not stop at the first answer | *"Why should it be twelve?"* | Asking so long that nothing gets checked |
| **SEQUENCE / WHAT HAPPENED BEFORE** | **Ronnie Pargeter** | Order of events; who was where, in what order | *"What happened before that?"* | Confusing a remembered order with a recorded one |
| **PHYSICAL EVIDENCE / WHAT CHANGED** | **Alfie Noakes** | The state of things; marks, weight, wear, absence | *"What's different about it now?"* | Trusting the object and ignoring the record |
| **DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE / WHAT DOES THE RECORD SAY** | **Pearl Emanuel** | What is written down, by whom, when, and in which book | *"Where does it say that?"* | Trusting the record and ignoring the object |

Full character records — families, addresses, provenance, and the documented
route that places each child in Corvesley — are in `WORLD-CORVESLEY.md` §3 and
`SCHOOL-CORVESLEY-CE.md` §6.

### 6.1 · The structural argument of the episode

Alfie's instrument and Pearl's instrument **disagree by design**: the record says
twelve, the objects say eleven. Ronnie's instrument is the only one that can
explain *how* they came apart. Bramble's instrument is the only one that keeps
them looking after the first plausible answer arrives.

**Rule:** the episode may never resolve by one child being right and the others
wrong. It resolves only when the four instruments are **combined**. Any draft in
which one child simply solves it is a failed draft.

### 6.2 · The accusation gate

Two hard rules, carried in every draft:

1. **No child names a suspect before the custody chain is walked end to end.**
2. When a question turns toward a person rather than a fact, **WYCK goes quiet**
   (W-6) — and Bramble notices the quiet. That is how the audience learns the
   rule without being told it.
